> ⚠️ **This is a beta.** It brings a redesigned desktop app and a reworked engine. Every change passes the automated test suite on Linux, macOS, Windows and Android, but this build has not yet been through real-device testing on every platform. If you want the proven version, stay on [v0.7.0](https://github.com/flowerpower584/fluxsync/releases/tag/v0.7.0). If you try the beta, thank you, and please [report anything odd](https://github.com/flowerpower584/fluxsync/issues/new).

**FluxSync copies on one device and pastes on another — over your own Wi-Fi, end-to-end encrypted, no account, no cloud.**

## What's new

### A new look on desktop
The macOS, Windows and Linux app is redesigned from scratch: a clear "linked / searching / off" headline, the link between your two devices drawn live, and three tabs — **Clipboard**, **Firewall**, **Devices**.
- **History you can actually use:** search as you type (Enter copies the best match), filter by links, code, images or pinned items, and press **Ctrl/⌘ + 1–9** to copy one of the last nine items.
- **Devices tab:** every paired device is listed, even when it's offline, and each one can be unpaired on its own.
- **Light, dark or system theme**, applied to every window at once.
- Faster: a busy history no longer slows the window down.

### Fixes you'll notice
- **Copying A, then B, then A again** now sends A the second time too (it used to be silently skipped), on desktop and Android.
- **Turning sync off really turns it off**, and turning it back on reconnects by itself.
- **"Unpair" reaches every device**, not just the main one.
- **Your favorites survive** when your other device has been away for a while. Only the non-pinned history is cleared.
- **Renaming a device** shows the new name on your other devices right away.
- Two items copied in quick succession can no longer land in the wrong order.
- Unpairing your only device no longer leaves it on screen as "Searching…".
- Medium-size texts (around 1 KB and up) sync reliably: the network format is now half the size.

### Security
- A recorded connection message can no longer be replayed on your network to cut your link.
- A device that hasn't been confirmed yet can no longer request items that weren't meant for it.
- Received images are decoded with strict size limits.
- Dependencies are updated, fixing 8 published security advisories (in rustls, tokio, h2 and others).

## Download

Pick the file for your device below.

| Device | File to download |
|---|---|
| **Android** (phone or tablet) | `FluxSync-v0.8.0-beta.1-arm64-v8a.apk` |
| **Mac with Apple chip** (M1, M2, M3…) | the `.zip` ending in `_aarch64.zip` |
| **Mac with Intel chip** | the `.zip` ending in `_x64.zip` |
| **Windows** (most PCs) | the file ending in `_x64-setup.exe` |
| **Windows on ARM** | the file ending in `_arm64-setup.exe` |
| **Linux** (Ubuntu, Debian…) | the `.deb` file |
| **Linux** (any distribution) | the `.AppImage` file |

The [README](https://github.com/flowerpower584/fluxsync#readme) walks through installing and pairing, step by step.

**Upgrading from v0.7.0:** install over your current version. Your pairings and history are kept, and a v0.7.0 device can still sync with a beta one while you upgrade them one by one. On Android, if the install is refused, uninstall v0.7.0 first; you will then need to pair again.

## Good to know
- **The apps aren't signed yet** (that needs paid Apple and Windows certificates). On **Mac**, use the `Install FluxSync.command` inside the zip; it takes care of the "app is damaged" warning. On **Windows**, click **More info → Run anyway** the first time.
- **On Android**, FluxSync asks to be turned on under **Settings → Accessibility**. That is the only way Android lets an app see your copies while it's in the background. [What it does and doesn't do](https://github.com/flowerpower584/fluxsync/blob/main/docs/WHY-ACCESSIBILITY.md).
- Both devices need to be on the **same network** (or on the same [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) network).
- Image sync still has rough edges between two computers: transparent images can paste with a white background, and copying an image *file* sends its path rather than the picture.
